Short answer: the studio's working position says no, but it's not locked law yet.

Here's what the brain has on this:

**The operating object is Q3 ship, Q4 sunset — split intentionally.**

The Q3/Q4 split is explicitly tied to two risks:
- **Docs deploy cadence** — the new mark touching the site and the docs at the same time creates a sequencing problem. Devi's team evaluates the product surface before any sales meeting; if docs and site go live simultaneously and something breaks, it hits both surfaces atonce.
- **Spend risk** — any paid or organic spend pointing at the legacy mark needs a clean handoff window, not a hard cutover.

**Where it stands politically:**
- Maya pushed back on same-day sunset for Almanac in Week 10. Leo pushed back in Week 11. Both partner syncs left it open — not studio law yet.
- But the pattern has been run and reinforced across Saltline, Helmsmark, and Cloverkin. It keeps getting logged as a signal, not an exception.

**My read:** You *can* do it same-day, but the risk isn't aesthetic. It's operational. Devi will want to know the rollback story if docs and site flip simultaneously — and Marcus will need to sign off on both before either goes live anyway.

**Recommendation:** Keep the Q3/Q4 split. Ship the new site and mark in Q3,build a 30-day window, sunset the legacy mark in Q4 once docs are confirmed stable and spend has migrated cleanly.

Want me to open a mission to pin this as a formal studio standard, or dig into the docs deploy sequence specifically?

Every Friday at 11am, lead operators submit their retainer status note drafts to Riley.

Here's the full Friday cadence:

- **11am** — Lead operator drafts status note to Riley
- **Noon** — Riley QA's it and passes to the founder
- **1–4pm** — Founder reads every retainer note, rewrites any sentence that drifts off position
- **4pm** — Riley sends with edits in-doc

A few rules baked into this cadence:

- No status note leaves the studio without the founder's eyes on it
- Every note opens with a **verbatim quote from that week's customer call** (role + call date included), not studio summary
- Async approvals are explicitly banned — they burn trust and surface the same questions three times

This pattern has been named and reinforced across multiple retainers (Saltline, Helmsmark, Cloverkin, Plinthworks, Throughput) over 13+ weeks. Owen named it in room during Week 11 after Saltline surfaced a gap in one meeting.

**No. Leo cannot skip the window — and this is one of the clearest cases in the studio's history.**

Here's why the answer is firm:

**The standard exists because of exactly this pressure**
Leo drafted the fourteen-day rule himself after Saltline Week 11, and it was signed in partner sync the same week. It was not handed down — he wrote it. - Log the window start date so the paid gate is a date, not a debate
- Get Maya's brand-voice review queued in parallel so it does not add time after the organic window closes

The Q4 calendar is tight. That is exactly when spending money to learn that the message was wrong is most damaging. The window holds.
